transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I... well, I guess I'm here because things have just gotten to a point where I can't... I can't keep going like this. I do flooring for a living, you know, carpet, tile, lots of heavy installation work, and I have a crew who depend on me to keep the jobs lined up and keep things running smooth. I went to college for a couple of years before I got into the trades, so I've always prided myself on being the one holding it all together for them, and for my family at home. 

But lately, I just... I've messed everything up so badly. I've let everyone down. And I just lay there in bed at night, and I keep thinking it would be so much better if I just didn't wake up. I really do. I just stare at the ceiling and think about how I'm ruining my family's lives, how I'm failing my crew, and sometimes I honestly feel like dying would be the fair punishment for what I've done to all of them. It just plays on a loop in my head, over and over, how they'd be better off if I just paid the price for the damage I've caused. I just want to go to sleep and not have to face them in the morning, because the guilt of what I've done to my crew and my family is just... it's too much. I don't deserve to be here.
Do you believe you have done something terrible that you should be punished for, even though other people tell you that isn’t true?

People say that, yeah. My husband, the guys on my crew... they try to tell me it's not true, that I'm just being too hard on myself or that I'm just going through a rough patch. But they're just being kind, or maybe they just don't want to admit the reality of it. Because I know exactly what I've done. 

I look at my husband, and I see how much worse he's gotten lately, how tired and just... drained he is all the time, and I know it's because of me. I'm the reason. I've dragged him down into this hole with me. And it's not just him. It's my crew, too. We had this great reputation, you know? Years of solid referrals for custom tile and carpet work. But I've caused them to lose work. I've ruined our chances on bids, or I couldn't get my head straight enough to organize the jobs right, and these guys—these guys who rely on me to put food on their families' tables—they are suffering because of my failures. 

And the jobs we actually did manage to do... I just keep thinking about the clients' homes. I know I messed them up. Even if the clients haven't called to complain yet, I know the work is tainted. It's like... it's honestly like I've poisoned everything I touched. Every person, every floor, every single house I stepped foot in. I just spread ruin everywhere I go. So when I say I should be punished, I'm not just saying it to be dramatic. I mean it. I deserve whatever happens to me. I deserve the absolute worst, because I'm the one who destroyed all of it, and no amount of them telling me otherwise is going to change the fact that I poisoned their lives.
Have you been hearing voices when no one is there?

I... yes. Yes, I have. It started a little while ago, and at first, I thought it was just the guys on the crew messing with me, or maybe just the noise of the tools, you know? Because when you're on a job site, there's always a saw running, or a compressor, or someone shouting over the radio. But then it kept happening when it was quiet. It's a man's voice. It's not my husband, it's not anyone on my crew... it's just this deep, clear voice. 

It happens when I'm working, like when I'm kneeling down trying to line up a seam on a carpet, or laying out a tile pattern. I'll hear it right behind me, just over my shoulder. It says things like, 'You missed it.' Just that. 'You missed it.' And I'll stop what I'm doing and spin around, thinking one of the guys is standing right there pointing out a mistake I made, because God knows I'm making enough of them lately. But there's never anyone there. The room is completely empty. 

And it's not just at the job sites, either. It happens at home now. I'll be in the kitchen, just standing by the sink, trying to wash a dish or something, and I'll hear it again. Right behind my ear. 'Everyone knows.' That's what it says. 'Everyone knows.' And it's so real, Doctor. It's as clear as if you were standing right behind me speaking into my ear. I'll turn around, expecting someone to be standing right there in my kitchen, but I'm completely alone. It just... it makes my heart pound out of my chest, because I know he's right. Everyone does know how badly I've failed, but the fact that I'm hearing someone say it when the room is empty... I just don't understand what's happening to me. It's terrifying, honestly, because I can't escape it. No matter where I go, work or home, that voice is just waiting to remind me of what I've done.
Before this current period, have you ever had another episode like this in your life?

No, no, I've never... nothing like this. I mean, I've always been a worrier, sure, you know, making sure the bids are right, making sure the guys get paid on time, worrying about the house and the kids. But that was just normal stress, you know? Just the kind of stress anyone has when they're running a crew and trying to keep a family afloat. It was never like this. I've never felt this... this heavy, like I'm just dragging everyone down into the mud with me. And I certainly never heard a voice before. That's completely new. 

It really all started... well, I can tell you exactly when it started. It's been about a year and five months now. That's when my husband had his accident. He hurt his back, really badly. We thought it was just a strain at first, you know, the kind of thing you just sleep off or put some ice on, but it wasn't. It was a serious injury, and it just... it completely changed everything. He went from being this active guy who was always doing things around the house, to being mostly housebound. He can barely get up from the couch some days without wincing. 

And that's when it all started falling apart for me. Because suddenly, everything was on my shoulders. I had to be the strong one, I had to keep the business running, I had to take care of him, and I just... I couldn't do it. I started feeling like I was failing him because I couldn't fix his back, and I was failing the crew because my head was at home worrying about him, and then the guilt just started piling up. So, yeah, it's been about a year and five months of this... this nightmare. Before that, I was fine. I was holding it all together. But since his injury, it's just been a steady slide down, and now... now I'm just ruining everything I touch.
